p:cNvPr.descr: The chromosomal DNA molecule cleavage. There is a chromosomal DNA strand. The strand is divided into multiple colored blocks. On the far left is a yellow block that takes up 3 nucleotides on each strand. There are 3 dashes, then the sequence GGT on the top strand, then 3 dashes and the sequence CCA. To the right is an orange section that contains a G on the top strand and the sequence CTTAA on the bottom, forming an L shape. To the right, there is a red block containing the top strand sequence AATTC; on the bottom is a lone G. The line between the orange and red sections on the top strand is labeled the cleavage site. To the right of the red block is a long lilac-colored section with top sequence AGC . . . TAG and bottom sequence TCG . . . ATC. To the right is a short orchid-colored section with sequence CAG on the top strand and sequence GTC on the bottom strand. Above, recognition sequences are labeled and indicated as being the red block on the left and the orchid-colored section on the right. To the right of the orchid block is a purple block with sequence CTG on top and GAC on bottom. The line between the orchid and purple blocks is labeled the cleavage site. To the right is a yellow block with top sequence TAGC--- and bottom sequence ATCG---. The dashed line to the right of each sequence shows that it continues on. Two small black arrows on the bottom also point up at the bottom of each cleavage site. Two down arrows point from each cleavage site. The left arrow is labeled EcoRI restriction endonuclease in blue. The right arrow is labeled Pvull restriction endonuclease in blue. Below, the DNA strand has been separated at the 2 cleavage sites into three parts. The left section has yellow and orange blocks, the middle section has the red, lilac, and orchid blocks, and the right section has the purple and yellow blocks. The left cleavage site is labeled (a) sticky ends underneath; the right cleavage site is labeled (b) blunt ends. Two arrows come from each cleavage site and merge down into a single arrow. There is a convergent arrow showing the addition of a vector, left. The vector is an unfinished ring, mostly yellow, with a staggered orange end and an even purple end. It is labeled “plasmid cloning vector cleaved with EcoRi and Pvull in the center. It is being added along with DNA ligase, shown in blue on the right. At the bottom is a completely closed vector, with the newly cleaved DNA segment filling the space in the vector. Now the orange sticky end of the vector is attached to the red sticky end of the recognition sequence. Between them are the lilac and orchid blocks, then the dark purple block attached to the yellow vector.
